findings.evidence: "The stipend clock resumes on their first day back."
findings.fix: Clarify the intended policy: for example, "Employees receive their next available stipend allocation during the following benefit year" or specify how the benefit year is calculated for returning employees.
findings.violation: The phrase "stipend clock resumes" is unclear about whether employees receive a fresh annual stipend allocation after leave or their previous benefit year continues.

findings.evidence: "However, an incomplete request pauses the timeline until the missing item arrives. The requester gets an automatic reminder after three days."
findings.fix: Specify the trigger point: "The requester gets an automatic reminder after three days of the request being marked incomplete."
findings.violation: It is unclear whether the three-day reminder timer starts from the original submission date or from when the request becomes incomplete.

findings.evidence: "A photo of the receipt is enough for most requests."
findings.fix: Either clarify which request types require original receipts or state definitively: "A photo of the receipt is sufficient for all requests."
findings.violation: "Most requests" implies some requests require different documentation, but the policy does not specify which requests fall into this category or what documentation they require.

findings.evidence: "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.fix: Rewrite in third person: "Employees must keep their equipment in good working condition and the company may request a brief photo check once a year."
findings.violation: This sentence shifts from third-person perspective throughout the document to second-person ("You," "we"), creating inconsistency in tone.

findings.evidence: "Also, you submit the request in the portal. You track its status there until the payment clears."
findings.fix: Change to third person: "Employees submit the request in the portal and track its status there until the payment clears."
findings.violation: Uses second-person ("you") inconsistently with the rest of the document, which uses third-person throughout.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt."
findings.fix: Remove the comma: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility and uploading the receipt."
findings.violation: The comma before "and" creates awkward parallel structure in the sentence.

findings.evidence: Program Overview states "the IT asset group tracks the equipment catalog on the first business day of the month." Special Cases states "The finance liaison publishes the equipment catalog at the start of the fiscal year."
findings.fix: Consolidate into a single clear statement specifying who publishes the catalog and whether updates occur monthly, at fiscal year start, or both.
findings.location: Program Overview section and Special Cases section (conflicting statements)
findings.violation: These two statements describe different frequencies and responsible parties for catalog updates, creating contradictory information.
